Candidate.description: Declared by a source and not yet tested.

Proposed.description: Proposed for testing (for example paired with trajectories to compare).

Duplicate.description: Repeats an earlier declaration of the same pair (DUPLICATE_OF names it).

Conflicting.description: One side is declared against more than one identifier on the other.

Invalid.description: The declaration could not be read as a valid pairing (an impossible date, a malformed identifier); kept with its text as evidence.

Bound.description: Tested and bound: the identities are joined.

OneLeftManyRight.description: One left identifier is declared against several right identifiers.

ManyLeftOneRight.description: One right identifier is declared against several left identifiers.

ManyLeftManyRight.description: Several on each side are declared against each other.

Uncalibrated.description: Not measured against independent reference states, or measured and failed

Calibrated.description: Measured against independent reference states and passed

ScaledFit.description: The formal covariance of an orbit fit, multiplied by the realism factor measured for the source and the fit's class (SCALE_FACTOR)

SourceModel.description: The source's own empirical model of its element sets' errors, by orbit regime and element-set age

PooledModel.description: The empirical model pooled over all sources, for a source without its own model in the regime

EmpiricalHistoryShrunk.description: Empirical errors from this object's own element-set history, shrunk toward a population prior identified by MODEL_ID and REGIME. Later element sets are comparison states, not independent truth; history alone never establishes calibration. HISTORY_* and SHRINKAGE_WEIGHT carry fitting evidence; SAMPLES/OBJECTS/SCALE_FACTOR retain their meanings.

Ephemeris.description: Ephemerides: states over time, from an operator or a precise-orbit service

Observation.description: Observations (ranges, angles, other measurements) that states are estimated from

Reference.description: Reference registers of sites and facilities (status, dates, identity)

Unspecified.description: Not stated. Never a grant: treated as CiteOnly.

Reproducible.description: The records may be republished, with the credit the terms ask.

CiteOnly.description: The records are computed on and cited, never republished.

ShareAlike.description: The records may be republished under the same terms, which every derived record carries.

NonCommercial.description: The records may be republished for non-commercial use only.

TRUE_OF_EPOCH_ECLIPTIC.description: True ecliptic of a fixed reference epoch.

BODY_FIXED.description: Axes rotating with the body named by AXIS_REFERENCE_BODY_NAIF_ID, per its published rotation elements.

BODY_INERTIAL.description: Non-rotating axes aligned with the reference body's equator and prime meridian at the reference epoch.

OBJECT_REFERENCED.description: Axes built from the relative geometry of two named objects; see RFMObjectReferencedAxes.

LOCAL_ALIGNED_CONSTRAINED.description: Axes built by aligning one vector and constraining a second; see RFMLocalAlignedConstrainedAxes.

BODY_EQUATOR.description: Axes in the reference body's equatorial plane at the requested epoch.

SOLAR_ECLIPTIC_MAGNETOSPHERIC.description: Solar-ecliptic magnetospheric axes: X toward the Sun, Z along the ecliptic north, commonly abbreviated GSE.

SOLAR_MAGNETOSPHERIC.description: Solar-magnetospheric axes: X toward the Sun, Z in the plane containing the body magnetic dipole, commonly abbreviated GSM.

TOPOCENTRIC.description: Local horizon axes at a surface site; the site is carried on RFMOrigin.

BODY_SPIN_SUN.description: Axes fixed by the body spin axis and the body-to-Sun direction.

EPHEMERIS_KERNEL_DEFINED.description: Axes defined by a loaded ephemeris/orientation kernel; identified by KERNEL_FRAME_NAME / KERNEL_FRAME_ID on RFMCoordinateSystem.

MEAN_OF_DATE_EQUATOR_FK5.description: LEGACY, retained and NAMED rather than left implicit: mean equator of date computed with the IAU-76/FK5 precession theory instead of the IAU-2006/2000A chain. Results differ from MEAN_OF_DATE_EQUATOR at the milliarcsecond level and the two are not interchangeable.

TRUE_OF_DATE_EQUATOR_FK5.description: LEGACY, retained and NAMED: true equator of date computed with the IAU-76/FK5 precession-nutation theory. See MEAN_OF_DATE_EQUATOR_FK5.

TRUE_OF_DATE_EQUATOR_IERS1996.description: True equator of date computed with the IERS Conventions (1996) reduction (IERS Technical Note 21): IAU 1976 precession, IAU 1980 nutation with the observed celestial pole offsets applied. Distinct from TRUE_OF_DATE_EQUATOR_FK5 (no offsets) and TRUE_OF_DATE_EQUATOR (IAU-2006/2000A).

TRUE_OF_DATE_EQUATOR_IERS2003.description: True equator of date computed with the IERS Conventions (2003) reduction (IERS Technical Note 32): IAU 2000A nutation on the IAU 1976 precession with the IAU 2000 precession-rate corrections. The mean-of-date equator under this reduction is MEAN_OF_DATE_EQUATOR_FK5.

TOPOCENTRIC_EAST_NORTH_UP.description: Topocentric East-North-Up axes at a surface site; the site is carried on RFMOrigin. TOPOCENTRIC (20) does not fix the axis order; this does.

TOPOCENTRIC_NORTH_EAST_DOWN.description: Topocentric North-East-Down axes at a surface site.

TOPOCENTRIC_SOUTH_EAST_ZENITH.description: Topocentric South-East-Zenith axes at a surface site.

ORBITAL_VELOCITY_NORMAL_CONORMAL.description: Orbital axes from the object's state: X along the velocity, Z along the orbit normal, Y completing the right-handed set (VNC). The object is the origin body of the coordinate system.

ORBITAL_RADIAL_TRANSVERSE_NORMAL.description: Orbital axes from the object's state: X radial (outward), Z along the orbit normal, Y transverse completing the set (RTN, also RSW).

ORBITAL_LOCAL_VERTICAL_LOCAL_HORIZONTAL.description: Orbital axes from the object's state: Z toward the central body (nadir), Y opposite the orbit normal, X completing the set (LVLH).

GALACTIC.description: IAU 1958 Galactic longitude/latitude axes, Hipparcos realization: NGP RA = 192.85948 deg, Dec = +27.12825 deg; l_Omega = 32.93192 deg. ESA SP-1200 (1997), Vol. 1, Section 1.5.3. Cartesian X points to l=0,b=0, Y to l=90,b=0, Z to the north Galactic pole (right-handed). This fixes orientation only, not the origin or the direction of Sgr A*. Explicit Galactocentric parameters select the derived orientation documented on ROLL_DEG; choosing an origin alone never rotates the axes. See Liu, Zhu & Zhang (2011), A&A 526, A16, on the definition and its realization in ICRS; do not substitute a newly fitted Galactic plane.

CELESTIAL_BODY.description: The centre of mass of a single celestial body.

BARYCENTRE.description: The barycentre of a named system of bodies.

LIBRATION_POINT.description: A libration (Lagrange) point of a two-body system.

SPACE_OBJECT.description: Another tracked space object, identified by OBJECT_ID.

GROUND_SITE.description: A fixed site on a body surface, identified by SITE_ID and the geodetic fields on RFMOrigin.

GALACTIC_CENTER.description: Galactic center at Sgr A*. Its ICRS direction, solar distance, height, roll and velocity are explicit parameters on RFMCoordinateSystem. No ephemeris body code is implied by this origin.

ORBIT_NORMAL.description: Orbit normal, RADIAL crossed into VELOCITY.

STATE_TRANSFORM.description: Transform a full state (position AND velocity) from SOURCE_COORDINATE_SYSTEM to TARGET_COORDINATE_SYSTEM at EPOCH, expressed in TARGET_REPRESENTATION.

FRAME_ROTATION.description: Return only the rotation from SOURCE_COORDINATE_SYSTEM to TARGET_COORDINATE_SYSTEM at EPOCH, with its time derivative and the angular velocity of the target axes. No state is required.

STATE_REPRESENTATION_CONVERT.description: Convert a state between element sets within ONE coordinate system.

UNSUPPORTED_AXIS_TYPE.description: The provider does not implement the requested axis set.

UNSUPPORTED_STATE_REPRESENTATION.description: The provider does not implement the requested element set.

MISSING_EOP_DATA.description: The axis chain needs Earth-orientation data that was not supplied or does not span EPOCH. The provider MUST fail here rather than silently extrapolate.

SINGULAR_ELEMENT_SET.description: The state is at a singularity of the requested element set (for example e -> 0 for Keplerian). The provider MUST report this rather than substitute a different element set.

KEPLERIAN.description: SMA, ECC, INC, RAAN, AOP, TA.

MODIFIED_KEPLERIAN.description: RadPer, RadApo, INC, RAAN, AOP, TA.

SPHERICAL_AZFPA.description: RMAG, RA, DEC, VMAG, azimuth, flight-path angle.

SPHERICAL_RADEC.description: RMAG, RA, DEC, VMAG, right ascension of velocity, declination of velocity.

EQUINOCTIAL.description: SMA, h, k, p, q, mean longitude.

MODIFIED_EQUINOCTIAL.description: p, f, g, h, k, true longitude.

ALTERNATE_EQUINOCTIAL.description: Equinoctial variant using mean motion in place of the semi-major axis.

DELAUNAY.description: Delaunay canonical variables l, g, h, L, G, H.

PLANETODETIC.description: Geodetic latitude/longitude/height with the horizon velocity triple.

BROUWER_MEAN_SHORT.description: Brouwer-Lyddane mean elements, short-period terms only.

BROUWER_MEAN_LONG.description: Brouwer-Lyddane mean elements, short and long period terms.

SCLK.description: Spacecraft Clock (receiver) (requires rules for interpretation in ICD)

A1.description: Atomic time scale of the reference atomic-time network, offset from International Atomic Time by the fixed constant A1 - TAI = 0.0343817 s exactly. Appended last; never reorder or reuse existing values.

GNSS_WEEK_SECONDS.description: GNSS week number plus seconds within the week.

CCSDS_TIME_CODE.description: CCSDS binary time-code field with preamble metadata.

MISSION_ELAPSED_SECONDS.description: Seconds from an application-defined mission epoch.

INVALID_INPUT.description: Input epoch or requested representation is invalid.

UNSUPPORTED_TIME_SYSTEM.description: Requested source or target time system is not supported.

LEAP_SECOND_DATA_REQUIRED.description: Conversion requires leap-second data that was not available.

EOP_DATA_REQUIRED.description: Conversion requires Earth-orientation data that was not available.

OUT_OF_RANGE.description: Requested instant is outside the supported conversion range.

SPACE_POINT.description: A point with an ephemeris but no vehicle properties: a celestial body, a barycentre, or a libration point.

METRE_SQUARED_PER_KILOGRAM.description: Area-to-mass ratio and ballistic coefficient reciprocal.

FRAME_INDEPENDENT.description: The value is the same in every coordinate system: mass, duration, a tank pressure.

COORDINATE_SYSTEM_DEPENDENT.description: The value depends on the full coordinate system, axes and origin.

CENTRAL_BODY_DEPENDENT.description: The value depends on the central body alone and not on the axes: the classical element set of a two-body orbit about a named body.

SURFACE_SITE_DEPENDENT.description: The value depends on a surface site as well as a body.

SECOND_OBJECT_DEPENDENT.description: The value depends on a second object as well as the owner.

DECLARED_UNAVAILABLE.description: The name is ratified and reserved, and the publisher REFUSES it with NOT_IMPLEMENTED. UNAVAILABLE_REASON states what is missing. A publisher MUST NOT substitute a neighbouring quantity.

DEPRECATED.description: Evaluated, but superseded; a consumer SHOULD migrate to the parameter named in SUPERSEDED_BY.

UNKNOWN_PARAMETER.description: The name does not resolve in the publisher's catalog.

NOT_IMPLEMENTED.description: The name resolves and is DECLARED_UNAVAILABLE.

MISSING_DEPENDENCY.description: A coordinate system, central body, site or second object the parameter requires was not supplied.

MISSING_OWNER_OBJECT.description: The owning object or hardware item named on the request is not present.

SINGULAR_AT_STATE.description: The parameter is undefined at this state: a node angle at zero inclination, an argument of periapsis at zero eccentricity.

OUT_OF_DOMAIN.description: The parameter is defined only on a regime this state is not in: a launch asymptote on a bound orbit.

GOAL_NOT_ATTAINED.description: A stopping condition was never attained inside the requested interval.

CCSDS_RDM_KVN.description: CCSDS Reentry Data Message, keyword-value notation.

SENTINEL_EOF_XML.description: ESA Earth Explorer orbit file in XML (Sentinel-1, -2 and -3 AUX_POEORB, AUX_RESORB and AUX_PREORB).

NAIF_CK_DAF.description: NAIF C-kernel: a DAF holding pointing (attitude) segments.

PCK_DAF.description: NAIF binary Planetary Constants Kernel: a DAF holding body orientation as Chebyshev segments (data types 2, 3 and 20), with no size or shape data; e.g. the Moon's principal-axis frame in moon_pa_de440_*.bpc (NAIF, PCK Required Reading).

PROVIDER_DEFINED.description: A container outside this roster. PROVIDER_DEFINED_FORMAT_NAME states which; a producer never reuses a neighbouring member instead.

IERS_C04_14.description: IERS EOP 14 C04, the long-term combined solution (e.g. eopc04_14_IAU2000.62-now.txt).

IERS_C04_20.description: IERS EOP 20 C04, the ITRF2020-based combined solution.

IERS_BULLETIN_A.description: IERS Bulletin A rapid service / prediction.

FINALS2000A.description: USNO/IERS finals2000A combined rapid + prediction file.

OTHER.description: A series not covered above; identify it in a producer-defined way.

PROVIDER_INTERPOLATED.description: Interpolated by the upstream data provider rather than the issuing observatory. Wire value 4 is unchanged from prior releases.

ECLIPSE.description: Passage of the target through the shadow of one or more occulting bodies.

CONTACT.description: Visibility of the target from a surface site, subject to a horizon or mask constraint.

INTRUSION.description: Entry of a body or object into a sensor field of view.

APSIDES.description: Passage of the target through an apsis of its orbit.

NODE_CROSSING.description: Passage of the target through the node line of a stated coordinate system.

PARAMETER_CONDITION.description: The generic locator: a condition on any $PCE catalog parameter. Altitude crossings, latitude crossings and beta-angle limits are this class, not classes of their own.

LATITUDE_EXTREMUM.description: Passage of the target through a maximum or a minimum of its geocentric latitude: the zero of the latitude rate, which no catalog parameter is.

UMBRA.description: Total occultation of the illuminating body.

PENUMBRA.description: Partial occultation of the illuminating body.

ANTUMBRA.description: The occulting body is fully inside the illuminating body disc.

RISE.description: The target crossed the constraint boundary into visibility.

SET.description: The target crossed the constraint boundary out of visibility.

ENTRY.description: Entry into a bounded volume or field of view.

EXIT.description: Exit from a bounded volume or field of view.

ASCENDING_NODE.description: Node crossing with the out-of-plane component increasing.

DESCENDING_NODE.description: Node crossing with the out-of-plane component decreasing.

CYLINDRICAL.description: The occulting body casts a cylinder; no penumbra exists.

CONICAL.description: A single cone; umbra and penumbra are distinguished.

DUAL_CONE.description: Umbra and penumbra cones evaluated separately, admitting antumbra.

NO_CORRECTION.description: Geometric positions at the same instant.

LIGHT_TIME.description: Positions corrected for one-way signal travel time.

LIGHT_TIME_AND_STELLAR_ABERRATION.description: Light time and the observer's transverse motion.

CONIC.description: A circular cone about the boresight, bounded by CONE_HALF_ANGLE_RAD.

RECTANGULAR.description: A rectangular pyramid about the boresight, bounded by the two half-angles.

CUSTOM_MASK.description: A custom boundary carried as a boresight-relative angular mask.

EVENT_EXTREMUM.description: The instant of the event's extremum: deepest obscuration, peak elevation, closest approach.

INTERIOR.description: A sample inside the event that is none of the above.

UNSUPPORTED_LOCATOR_CLASS.description: The provider does not implement the requested locator class.

MISSING_CONFIGURATION.description: The configuration table matching LOCATOR_CLASS was absent.

MISSING_EPHEMERIS.description: The state source did not span the requested interval.

MISSING_EOP_DATA.description: The geometry needs Earth-orientation data that was not supplied or does not span the interval.

PARAMETER_UNAVAILABLE.description: A generic condition names a parameter the provider cannot evaluate, or one that does not support a stopping condition.

ROOT_REFINEMENT_FAILED.description: A crossing was bracketed but the refinement did not converge to REFINEMENT_TOLERANCE_SECONDS. The provider MUST report this rather than emit an unconverged epoch.

BUDGET_EXCEEDED.description: The run hit MAXIMUM_EVENTS or its evaluation budget before reaching SCAN_STOP_EPOCH; the events reported are a prefix, not the whole answer.

UNSPECIFIED.description: The receiving module's own theory. A module that offers several reads UNSPECIFIED as the one it ingests element sets with (the advanced propagator reads it as SGP4XP).

SGP4.description: Mean-element theory of SPACETRACK REPORT No. 3 (SGP4 near Earth, SDP4 deep space).

SGP4XP.description: SGP4 with extended perturbations (SGP4-XP, as published in the 2022 astrodynamics conference literature); the same value as $MET SGP4XP.

FFM.description: Numerical integration of the equations of motion under the full force model of PCFForceModel (profile FFM-1).

KEPLER.description: Two-body (Keplerian) motion about the central body.

NEAREST.description: The set whose epoch is nearest the request time (the default).

LATEST_BEFORE.description: The latest set whose epoch is at or before the request time.

SMOOTHSTEP.description: Smoothstep weight on the two propagated states (the default).

HERMITE.description: Cubic Hermite matching of position and velocity across the window.

UNSPECIFIED.description: The provider's own rule (the numerical propagator refuses, the advanced mean-element propagator chains forecasts).

REFUSE.description: Refuse an arc that reaches past the rows (space-weather-out-of-range).

FORECAST_CHAIN.description: Observed rows, then the three-day forecast, then the 45-day forecast, then the solar-cycle climatology; each hand-off is blended over one day and every evaluation names its tier.

UNSPECIFIED.description: Infer: PCFSpaceWeather when the force model carries it, else the daily rows supplied with the request.

CONSTANT.description: PCFSpaceWeather, held for the whole arc.

RECORDS.description: Daily rows supplied with the request ($SPW rows; the JB2008 indices for the JB2008 atmosphere).

NONE.description: Density as the atmosphere model gives it.

DCA_COMMON_MODE.description: The open-DCA common-mode correction published as $DCL: model density times exp(s(t)), s the log-density scale of the published nodes.

NONE.description: Atmosphere co-rotating with the central body, no wind.

HWM14.description: The HWM14 empirical horizontal wind model (Drob et al. 2015, Earth and Space Science 2, 301-319).

UNSPECIFIED.description: The provider's own source, named in EPHEMERIS_SOURCE.

ANALYTIC_SERIES.description: A closed-form analytic series (low precision, no kernel to load).

PLANETARY_KERNEL.description: A planetary ephemeris kernel (SPK), named in EPHEMERIS_SOURCE.

APSIS.description: g = r . v, the radial rate. INCREASING crossings are periapsis, DECREASING apoapsis.

PLANE_CROSSING.description: g = n . r for the plane through the central body's center with normal PLANE_NORMAL (absent: the pole of the request's axes, which makes the crossings the nodes). INCREASING crossings are ascending, DECREASING descending.

TRUE_ANOMALY.description: g = the true anomaly minus ANGLE_RAD, wrapped to (-pi, pi]. INCREASING.

ARGUMENT_OF_LATITUDE.description: g = the argument of latitude minus ANGLE_RAD, wrapped to (-pi, pi]. INCREASING.

LATITUDE_EXTREMUM.description: g = r^2 d(z)/dt - z (r . v) with z the component along the pole of the request's axes: the zero of the rate of the geocentric latitude. DECREASING crossings are maxima, INCREASING minima.

UMBRA.description: g = the angular separation of the Sun and the central body's centers minus the difference of their apparent radii, positive in light (the umbra of the conical model). DECREASING is entry, INCREASING exit.

PENUMBRA.description: g = the same separation minus the sum of the apparent radii (the penumbra boundary).

CLOSEST_APPROACH.description: g = (r - r2) . (v - v2), r2 and v2 the position and velocity of the trajectory on the input port named by SECOND_TRAJECTORY_PORT. INCREASING crossings are minima of the range. The $OEM must cover the propagated arc; the provider interpolates it by Hermite polynomials.

INCREASING.description: g goes from negative to positive.

DECREASING.description: g goes from positive to negative.

CONTINUE.description: The event is located and counted; it is not reported.

RECORD.description: The event is located, counted and reported; propagation continues.

STOP.description: The event is reported and the propagation ends there: the final sample is the state at the OCCURRENCE-th qualifying crossing.

PARAMETER.description: Push the value of PARAMETER at the integrated state, in the units of the $PCE catalog.

ADD.description: Pop two, push their sum, difference (second minus first popped), product or quotient.

MINIMUM.description: Pop two, push the lesser or the greater.

UNSPECIFIED.description: The grid template's frame; TEME without one.

TEME.description: True equator, mean equinox of date.

EME2000.description: Mean equator and equinox of J2000.0.

RK4.description: Classical fourth-order Runge-Kutta, fixed step INITIAL_STEP_SECONDS.

RK78.description: The same Fehlberg 7(8) pair under the name the full force model's catalog profile uses, adaptive.

RKDP87.description: Prince-Dormand 8(7), thirteen stages, "RK8(7)13M" (Prince and Dormand 1981, J. Comput. Appl. Math. 7), adaptive.

COWELL.description: Cowell's method: Cartesian position and velocity.

ENCKE.description: Encke's method: the deviation from a reference conic.

EQUINOCTIAL_VOP.description: Variation of parameters in equinoctial elements.

DOPRI5.description: Dormand-Prince 5(4), seven stages (Dormand and Prince 1980, J. Comput. Appl. Math. 6).

RK65.description: Prince-Dormand 6(5), eight stages, minimized error coefficients, "RK6(5)8M" (Prince and Dormand 1981, J. Comput. Appl. Math. 7).

RKV98.description: Verner's 9(8) pair, sixteen stages (Verner 2010, Numer. Algorithms 53).

RKN1210.description: Runge-Kutta-Nystrom 12(10), seventeen stages, for y'' = f(t, y) alone (Dormand, El-Mikkawy and Prince 1987, IMA J. Numer. Anal. 7). The acceleration must not depend on velocity, so a provider refuses it with drag.

GAUSS_JACKSON_8.description: Gauss-Jackson eighth-order summed multistep, predict-evaluate-correct, started by a Runge-Kutta run (Berry and Healy 2004, J. Astronaut. Sci. 52).

GAUSS_VOP.description: Gauss's variational equations in classical Keplerian elements. Integrates a reduced force model; FFM refuses it by name.

DROMO.description: DROMO, the regularized special-perturbation formulation (Pelaez, Hedo and Rodriguez de Andres 2007, Celest. Mech. Dyn. Astron. 97). FFM refuses it by name: its propagation does not reach the requested epoch to the integration tolerance.

STIEFEL.description: Stiefel-Scheifele regularized formulation in the fictitious time (Stiefel and Scheifele 1971, Linear and Regular Celestial Mechanics). FFM refuses it by name, as DROMO.

DOPRI853.description: Dormand-Prince 8(5,3), twelve stages (Hairer, Norsett and Wanner 1993, Solving Ordinary Differential Equations I).

EGM96.description: NGA EGM96 (Lemoine et al. 1998, NASA/TP-1998-206861), tide-free.

GRGM660PRIM.description: GRGM660PRIM (Lemoine et al. 2013, J. Geophys. Res. Planets 118), the Moon's field, in the Moon's principal-axis frame.

MRO120F.description: MRO120F (Konopliv et al. 2020, Geophys. Res. Lett. 47, doi:10.1029/2020GL090568), the Mars field, in the Mars-fixed frame of its PDS label.

JACCHIA_ROBERTS.description: Jacchia-Roberts (Roberts, Celestial Mechanics 4, 1971): the closed-form evaluation of Jacchia's static diffusion model with the constants NASA GTDS and GMAT use (inflection temperature, mean molecular mass and 100 km composition of Jacchia 1971, SAO SR 332; ATM's JR71). The drivers: F10.7 of the previous day, that day's 81-day centred average, and the three-hour Kp 6.7 h earlier (PRW.SPACE_WEATHER, or WEATHER's values held constant). A VCM's JACCHIA_70 is carried here.

JB2008.description: Jacchia-Bowman 2008 (Bowman et al., AIAA 2008-6438): solar indices and Dst-derived temperature change from the request's JB2008 indices.

MARS_EXPONENTIAL.description: Banded exponential atmosphere of Mars: the density falls as exp(-(h - h0) / H) through altitude bands (Vallado, Fundamentals of Astrodynamics and Applications, 4th ed., section 8.6), and it co-rotates with Mars.

UNKNOWN_ENTITY.description: One or more entity handles not found.

INVALID_EPOCH.description: Invalid epoch (NaN, out of range, before earliest init epoch, etc.).

OUTPUT_BUFFER_OVERFLOW.description: Output buffer too small for the requested count.

OMM.description: Source is an OMM (CCSDS mean elements) FlatBuffer.

TLE.description: Source is a raw TLE line pair (3LE supported via NAME).

PPE.description: Source is a PPE (polynomial ephemeris) FlatBuffer.

KEPLERIAN.description: Source is a single classical Keplerian element set.

ECOM2_D0.description: ECOM2 coefficients (PCFEcom2), in their order there.

Compatible.description: Trajectories agree within the tolerances (supports review; not proof).

Ambiguous.description: Agree, but another proposed pairing of the same identity also passes.

Insufficient.description: Could not be judged: different grids or frames, too short an arc, or supplied velocities inconsistent with the positions.

NoradFirst.description: NORAD number first, then international designator, then the source's native key (recipe version 1).

InternationalDesignator.description: International designator only; records without one stay unresolved (recipe version 2).

Selected.description: A record was selected and published.

IdentityConflict.description: Layers disagree on the object's identifiers; withheld until an override names a layer.

MissingDesignator.description: No valid international designator under the international-designator rule; withheld.

Selected.description: A state candidate within the maximum age was selected.

Stale.description: The configured sources' newest states are older than the maximum age.

Future.description: The configured sources have only states after the as-of time.

Missing.description: No configured source has a state for the object.

Covered.description: Exactly one source declares coverage of the object (or an override chose one).

Overlap.description: Several sources declare coverage and none was chosen.

Retired.description: Epoch before a maneuver that retires the products before it.

TooOld.description: Older than the policy's maximum age.

LowestMeasuredMedian.description: Lowest measured median error among the measured eligible candidates.

UnmeasuredFallbackOrder.description: No candidate measured; the source order decided.

Validated.description: Training and held-out residuals within the tolerance.

RequiresRefinement.description: Residuals exceed the tolerance; refine the state.

RejectedHoldoutRegression.description: Held-out RMS above the policy's maximum.

CandidateNeedsPropagation.description: A corrected state was proposed and must be re-propagated and validated.

Selected.description: At least one product kind has a selection.

Stale.description: Products exist but none is eligible.

OILIdentifier.description: One object identifier in one namespace.

NAMESPACE.description:
Namespace (catalog or provider) the identifier belongs to, e.g. "vimpel",
"NORAD", "COSPAR", "space-track", "esa-discos".

ID.description:
The identifier in canonical form (leading zeros removed for a number),
e.g. "12" for Vimpel "00012".

ID_AS_PRINTED.description:
The identifier exactly as the source printed it; empty when the same as
ID.

NORAD_CAT_ID.description:
NORAD catalog number when the namespace is NORAD or the identifier
resolves to one; 0 = none.

INTERNATIONAL_DESIGNATOR.description: International (COSPAR) designator when known, YYYY-NNNP; empty = none.

FIRST_DETECTED.description:
Date the source says the object was first detected under this
identifier, ISO 8601 calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD); empty when not stated
or not a valid date.

FIRST_DETECTED_AS_PRINTED.description:
The first-detection date as printed, when it is not a valid date (e.g.
"20239591"); empty otherwise.

TRAJECTORY_ID.description:
Identifier of a trajectory or state product of this identity that a test
of the link compares (an $XMT trajectory ID); empty = none.

SOURCE.description:
Kind of source of the declaration, e.g. "datefirst", "satcat",
"operator", "analyst".

RECORD_ID.description:
Immutable identifier of the source edition: a SHA-256 hex digest or CID
of the file or record.

LINE.description: 1-based line of the declaration in the source edition; 0 = not stated.

DECLARATIONS.description: Number of times the edition declares this pair (1 = once).

DATES_DIFFER.description: True when repeated declarations of the pair give different dates.

ORIGINAL.description: The declaration's text as printed, when kept (for an Invalid link).

OILLink.description: One candidate link between two identifiers.

LEFT.description: The identifier being linked (typically the provider-native one).

RIGHT.description: The identifier it is linked to (typically the reference catalog's).

Candidate.description: Declared by a source and not yet tested.

Proposed.description: Proposed for testing (for example paired with trajectories to compare).

Duplicate.description: Repeats an earlier declaration of the same pair (DUPLICATE_OF names it).

Conflicting.description: One side is declared against more than one identifier on the other.

Invalid.description: The declaration could not be read as a valid pairing (an impossible date, a malformed identifier); kept with its text as evidence.

Bound.description: Tested and bound: the identities are joined.

AMBIGUOUS.description:
True when either side belongs to a group that is not one-to-one; such a
link never binds without review.

DUPLICATE_OF.description: For a Duplicate, the LINE of the declaration it repeats; 0 = none.

REASON.description: Why the link has its status (human-readable); empty when Candidate.

OILConflict.description:
A group of identifiers declared against each other that is not
one-to-one.

LEFT_IDS.description: Left identifiers in the group, as "<namespace>:<id>".

RIGHT_IDS.description: Right identifiers in the group, as "<namespace>:<id>".

OneLeftManyRight.description: One left identifier is declared against several right identifiers.

ManyLeftOneRight.description: One right identifier is declared against several left identifiers.

ManyLeftManyRight.description: Several on each side are declared against each other.

OIL.description: Object Identity Link - one crosswalk of candidate links.

LEFT_NAMESPACE.description: Namespace of every LEFT identifier, when uniform.

RIGHT_NAMESPACE.description: Namespace of every RIGHT identifier, when uniform.

HEADER.description:
Header line of the source file as printed, e.g.
"Nvym t_det_v Nnor t_det_n".

SHA256.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the source edition (the RECORD_ID of its links).

BYTES.description: Size of the source edition, bytes.

DUPLICATE_LINES.description: Rows that repeated an earlier pair.

AMBIGUOUS_COUNT.description: Links in groups that are not one-to-one.

DATES_DIFFER_COUNT.description: Links whose repeated declarations give different dates.

UNREADABLE_DATE_COUNT.description: Links with a first-detection date that is not a valid date.

GENERATED_AT_MS.description: Unix milliseconds when the crosswalk was generated; 0 = unknown.

RULE.description:
The rule that produced the covariance. In a CCSDS covariance block,
Operator keeps the operator's COV_BASIS, ScaledFit is DETERMINED, and
SourceModel, PooledModel and EmpiricalHistoryShrunk are EMPIRICAL with
MODEL_ID as COV_BASIS_ID.

ScaledFit.description: The formal covariance of an orbit fit, multiplied by the realism factor measured for the source and the fit's class (SCALE_FACTOR)

SourceModel.description: The source's own empirical model of its element sets' errors, by orbit regime and element-set age

PooledModel.description: The empirical model pooled over all sources, for a source without its own model in the regime

EmpiricalHistoryShrunk.description: Empirical errors from this object's own element-set history, shrunk toward a population prior identified by MODEL_ID and REGIME. Later element sets are comparison states, not independent truth; history alone never establishes calibration. HISTORY_* and SHRINKAGE_WEIGHT carry fitting evidence; SAMPLES/OBJECTS/SCALE_FACTOR retain their meanings.

MODEL_ID.description:
Identifier of the error model (SourceModel, PooledModel) or of the
measured realism factor (ScaledFit) the covariance came from. Empty for
Operator. For EmpiricalHistoryShrunk, identifies the population prior;
EVIDENCE identifies the history estimator and its configuration.

REGIME.description: Orbit regime of the cell, as the model names it.

AGE_DAYS.description:
Age of the element set at the covariance's epoch, in days. NaN when the
covariance is not an element set's.

HORIZON_DAYS.description:
Prediction horizon of the cell, in days: the element-set age its
statistics were measured at. NaN when no cell applies.

MEASURED_LINEAGE.description:
Lineage of the reference data the cell was measured on (a PVN LINEAGE).
The test speaks for a covariance whose source has this lineage; for any
other lineage the numbers are the cell's, and CALIBRATION is Uncalibrated.

TEST_WINDOW.description:
Window of the held-out reference states the test used: an ISO 8601 UTC
interval, start/end.

MEAN_D2_OVER_3.description: Mean of d2/3 over the held-out samples. NaN when not measured.

COVERAGE_95.description:
Share of the held-out samples inside the 95 % region, 0 to 1. NaN when
not measured.

SAMPLES.description: Number of held-out samples the test used.

OBJECTS.description: Number of distinct objects the samples came from.

SCALE_FACTOR.description:
Factor the covariance was multiplied by to make it realistic. NaN when
none was applied.

CALIBRATION.description:
The verdict. Calibrated when MEAN_D2_OVER_3 lies in [0.8, 1.25] and
COVERAGE_95 in [0.93, 0.97], from at least 30 samples of at least 3
objects of MEASURED_LINEAGE; Uncalibrated otherwise, including a cell
never measured.

Uncalibrated.description: Not measured against independent reference states, or measured and failed

Calibrated.description: Measured against independent reference states and passed

EVIDENCE.description: Identifier of the report or record that holds the test.

HISTORY_SAMPLES.description:
Number of retained older/newer element-set residual pairs from this
object in the age bin containing AGE_DAYS, after rejection/clipping.
Zero means no retained pairs; never the held-out test count SAMPLES.

HISTORY_SETS.description:
Number of distinct older element sets contributing HISTORY_SAMPLES.
Zero means none; never the distinct calibration-object count OBJECTS.

HISTORY_WINDOW.description:
ISO 8601 UTC start/end interval spanning the element-set epochs used
in the object's history fit. Empty when no history was used. This is
training support, not TEST_WINDOW or the element-set age AGE_DAYS.

SHRINKAGE_WEIGHT.description:
Dimensionless population-prior fraction alpha in the covariance blend
P = (1-alpha) H + alpha P_prior, where H is the history error second
moment and P_prior includes the population model's realism scaling.
Range [0,1]: 0 is all history, 1 is all prior; NaN when not applicable
or unknown. For interpolation across bins, report the correspondingly
interpolated alpha. EVIDENCE must identify the estimator/configuration,
retained-count bin, participating bins and their weights so the blend
can be reconstructed; the scalar alone does not describe that mixture.
This is not SCALE_FACTOR, which multiplies a covariance. History-only
evidence leaves CALIBRATION Uncalibrated and test statistics unmeasured.

SOURCE_ID.description:
Publisher-stable, lowercase identifier of the source in the provider's
registry of sources.

SOURCE_KIND.description: What kind of data the source supplies.

Ephemeris.description: Ephemerides: states over time, from an operator or a precise-orbit service

Observation.description: Observations (ranges, angles, other measurements) that states are estimated from

Reference.description: Reference registers of sites and facilities (status, dates, identity)

ORIGINATOR.description:
Agency, operator or catalog that created the source data, as it names
itself. Not a message's CCSDS ORIGINATOR, which names who created the
message.

PROVIDER_ID.description:
Identifier of the provider that published the product, as the provider
names itself: the module, node or service that retrieved the source data.

PRODUCER.description:
Identifier of the software that made the product from the source data,
with its version when it has one.

LICENSE_CLASS.description: What the source's terms permit for the product.

Unspecified.description: Not stated. Never a grant: treated as CiteOnly.

Reproducible.description: The records may be republished, with the credit the terms ask.

CiteOnly.description: The records are computed on and cited, never republished.

ShareAlike.description: The records may be republished under the same terms, which every derived record carries.

NonCommercial.description: The records may be republished for non-commercial use only.

LICENSE_ID.description:
Identifier of the terms LICENSE_CLASS was read from: an SPDX license
identifier where one applies, else the identifier of the terms in the
provider's licence register.

LINEAGE.description:
Identifier of the lineage the source's data descends from. Sources that
republish one upstream share its lineage, so their products are not
independent of each other.

SIGMA_U.description: Position uncertainty along U, radial, in the UVW frame of this state (km, 1-sigma)

SIGMA_V.description: Position uncertainty along V, in-track, in the UVW frame of this state (km, 1-sigma)

SIGMA_W.description: Position uncertainty along W, cross-track, in the UVW frame of this state (km, 1-sigma)

MNV.description:
Spacecraft Maneuver

U, V and W are the UVW axes of an orbit state: U radial, along the position
vector away from the central body; W cross-track, along the orbit normal
(the direction of r x v); V in-track, W x U, completing the right-handed
frame. DELTA_VEL_U/V/W and DELTA_POS_U/V/W are in the UVW frame of the
pre-maneuver state at EVENT_START_TIME.

EVENT_ID.description:
Maneuver event identifier. Records of one event share it: a merged event
and the source records it combines.

MNVR_ACCELS.description:
Acceleration values (km/s^2): U, V and W per point, in the UVW frame of
the state at that point's MNVR_ACCEL_TIMES entry

SOURCED_DATA.description:
Sourced data references: identifiers of the records this one was
determined from (CIDv1 for records of this network), such as the source
records a merged event combines

PROVENANCE.description: Where the maneuver's data comes from and the terms it travels under.

RFMOrigin.description:
The point a coordinate system is centred on. Body and barycentre
identifiers are integer ephemeris body codes; text NAME is descriptive
only and is never the machine key.

CELESTIAL_BODY.description: The centre of mass of a single celestial body.

BARYCENTRE.description: The barycentre of a named system of bodies.

LIBRATION_POINT.description: A libration (Lagrange) point of a two-body system.

SPACE_OBJECT.description: Another tracked space object, identified by OBJECT_ID.

GROUND_SITE.description: A fixed site on a body surface, identified by SITE_ID and the geodetic fields on RFMOrigin.

GALACTIC_CENTER.description: Galactic center at Sgr A*. Its ICRS direction, solar distance, height, roll and velocity are explicit parameters on RFMCoordinateSystem. No ephemeris body code is implied by this origin.

CELESTIAL_BODY_ID.description: Ephemeris body code when KIND is CELESTIAL_BODY.

BARYCENTRE_ID.description: Ephemeris body code of the barycentre when KIND is BARYCENTRE.

LIBRATION_POINT.description: Which libration point, when KIND is LIBRATION_POINT.

LIBRATION_PRIMARY_ID.description: Ephemeris body code of the libration system primary.

LIBRATION_SECONDARY_ID.description: Ephemeris body code of the libration system secondary.

OBJECT_ID.description: Identifier of the space object when KIND is SPACE_OBJECT.

SITE_ID.description: Identifier of the surface site when KIND is GROUND_SITE.

SITE_BODY_ID.description: Ephemeris body code of the body the site sits on.

SITE_LATITUDE.description: Geodetic latitude of the site, degrees, positive north.

SITE_LONGITUDE.description: Geodetic longitude of the site, degrees, positive east.

SITE_ALTITUDE.description: Height of the site above the reference ellipsoid, metres.

RFMObjectReferencedAxes.description:
Axes built from the relative geometry of two objects. Exactly two of the
three axis assignments are independent; the third completes the triad.

ORBIT_NORMAL.description: Orbit normal, RADIAL crossed into VELOCITY.
Orbit normal, RADIAL crossed into VELOCITY.
Orbit normal, RADIAL crossed into VELOCITY.

RFMLocalAlignedConstrainedAxes.description:
Axes built by aligning one vector with a reference direction and using a
second vector as a constraint. Vectors are 3-element, expressed in the
coordinate system named by REFERENCE_COORDINATE_SYSTEM_NAME.

A fully specified coordinate system: an axis set, an origin, and the epoch
and time system the axis set is evaluated at. This is the unit a frames
consumer needs; the pre-existing RFMUnion members name an axis convention
alone and cannot express an origin.

BODY_INERTIAL.description: Non-rotating axes aligned with the reference body's equator and prime meridian at the reference epoch.

SOLAR_MAGNETOSPHERIC.description: Solar-magnetospheric axes: X toward the Sun, Z in the plane containing the body magnetic dipole, commonly abbreviated GSM.

TOPOCENTRIC.description: Local horizon axes at a surface site; the site is carried on RFMOrigin.

BODY_SPIN_SUN.description: Axes fixed by the body spin axis and the body-to-Sun direction.

MEAN_OF_DATE_EQUATOR_FK5.description: LEGACY, retained and NAMED rather than left implicit: mean equator of date computed with the IAU-76/FK5 precession theory instead of the IAU-2006/2000A chain. Results differ from MEAN_OF_DATE_EQUATOR at the milliarcsecond level and the two are not interchangeable.

TRUE_OF_DATE_EQUATOR_FK5.description: LEGACY, retained and NAMED: true equator of date computed with the IAU-76/FK5 precession-nutation theory. See MEAN_OF_DATE_EQUATOR_FK5.

TRUE_OF_DATE_EQUATOR_IERS1996.description: True equator of date computed with the IERS Conventions (1996) reduction (IERS Technical Note 21): IAU 1976 precession, IAU 1980 nutation with the observed celestial pole offsets applied. Distinct from TRUE_OF_DATE_EQUATOR_FK5 (no offsets) and TRUE_OF_DATE_EQUATOR (IAU-2006/2000A).

TRUE_OF_DATE_EQUATOR_IERS2003.description: True equator of date computed with the IERS Conventions (2003) reduction (IERS Technical Note 32): IAU 2000A nutation on the IAU 1976 precession with the IAU 2000 precession-rate corrections. The mean-of-date equator under this reduction is MEAN_OF_DATE_EQUATOR_FK5.

TOPOCENTRIC_EAST_NORTH_UP.description: Topocentric East-North-Up axes at a surface site; the site is carried on RFMOrigin. TOPOCENTRIC (20) does not fix the axis order; this does.

TOPOCENTRIC_NORTH_EAST_DOWN.description: Topocentric North-East-Down axes at a surface site.

TOPOCENTRIC_SOUTH_EAST_ZENITH.description: Topocentric South-East-Zenith axes at a surface site.

ORBITAL_VELOCITY_NORMAL_CONORMAL.description: Orbital axes from the object's state: X along the velocity, Z along the orbit normal, Y completing the right-handed set (VNC). The object is the origin body of the coordinate system.

ORBITAL_RADIAL_TRANSVERSE_NORMAL.description: Orbital axes from the object's state: X radial (outward), Z along the orbit normal, Y transverse completing the set (RTN, also RSW).

ORBITAL_LOCAL_VERTICAL_LOCAL_HORIZONTAL.description: Orbital axes from the object's state: Z toward the central body (nadir), Y opposite the orbit normal, X completing the set (LVLH).

GALACTIC.description: IAU 1958 Galactic longitude/latitude axes, Hipparcos realization: NGP RA = 192.85948 deg, Dec = +27.12825 deg; l_Omega = 32.93192 deg. ESA SP-1200 (1997), Vol. 1, Section 1.5.3. Cartesian X points to l=0,b=0, Y to l=90,b=0, Z to the north Galactic pole (right-handed). This fixes orientation only, not the origin or the direction of Sgr A*. Explicit Galactocentric parameters select the derived orientation documented on ROLL_DEG; choosing an origin alone never rotates the axes. See Liu, Zhu & Zhang (2011), A&A 526, A16, on the definition and its realization in ICRS; do not substitute a newly fitted Galactic plane.

AXIS_REFERENCE_BODY_ID.description:
Ephemeris body code whose equator/rotation defines the axes, for the
body-referenced axis types. Independent of ORIGIN.

EPOCH.description:
Reference epoch the axis set is evaluated at, ISO 8601. Required for the
of-date and of-epoch axis types; ignored by the inertial ones.

EPOCH_TIME_SYSTEM.description:
Time system the EPOCH is expressed in, named by the $TIM timingStandard
member name (for example "UTC", "TAI", "TT", "TDB", "A1").

KERNEL_FRAME_NAME.description: Kernel-declared frame name for EPHEMERIS_KERNEL_DEFINED axes.

KERNEL_FRAME_ID.description: Kernel-declared numeric frame id for EPHEMERIS_KERNEL_DEFINED axes.

EOP_DATA_SET_CID.description:
Content identifier of the Earth-orientation data set used to realise
this system, when the axis chain requires one. Recorded so that two
consumers can prove they used the same table rather than assume it.

GALCEN_RA_DEG.description:
ICRS right ascension of the Galactic center, degrees. NaN means absent.
Sgr A*: 17h45m40.0409s (Reid & Brunthaler 2004, ApJ 616, 872).

GALCEN_DEC_DEG.description:
ICRS declination of the Galactic center, degrees. NaN means absent.
Sgr A*: -29d00m28.118s (Reid & Brunthaler 2004, ApJ 616, 872).

GALCEN_DISTANCE_PC.description:
Sun-to-Galactic-center distance R0, parsecs. NaN means absent.
Example: 8178 pc (GRAVITY Collaboration 2019, A&A 625, L10).

Z_SUN_PC.description:
Solar height above the Galactic midplane, parsecs, positive north.
NaN means absent; example: 20.8 pc (Bennett & Bovy 2019, MNRAS 482, 1417).

ROLL_DEG.description:
Roll angle in degrees in the Astropy Galactocentric convention.
NaN means absent, not zero. With GALACTIC axes, the five explicit scalar
parameters define a derived Galactocentric orientation: X points from
the Sun toward the center's projection in the midplane, Y follows
Galactic rotation, and Z completes a right-handed triad toward Galactic
north. This parameterized orientation is independent of ORIGIN; with
GALACTIC_CENTER the Sun lies at X=-sqrt(R0^2-Z_SUN_PC^2), Y=0, Z=Z_SUN_PC.
All five scalars must be finite for a spatial Galactocentric transform,
with R0 > 0 and abs(Z_SUN_PC) <= R0; none has an assumed default.

V_SUN_KMS.description:
Total solar velocity [v_X,v_Y,v_Z] in km/s in the resulting Galactocentric
axes, including circular motion (not just peculiar U,V,W). Exactly three
components when present; omit the vector when unknown, or use NaN for
an unknown component. A velocity transform requires all three finite.
Schonrich, Binney & Dehnen (2010), MNRAS 403, 1829, constrain peculiar
motion; Reid & Brunthaler (2020), ApJ 892, 39, constrain Sgr A* motion.
Publishers must state their adopted total velocity; no default is implied.

PCEParameterCondition.description:
A predicate on a named parameter: the parameter attains GOAL_VALUE, in
DIRECTION, for the OCCURRENCE-th time. This is the ONE spelling of a
stopping condition and of a generic event function; $EVL references it
rather than minting a second one.

GOAL_VALUE.description: Value the parameter must attain, in the parameter's own SI unit.

ANY_CROSSING.description: Any crossing of GOAL_VALUE, in either direction.

INCREASING.description: Only a crossing with the parameter increasing through GOAL_VALUE.

DECREASING.description: Only a crossing with the parameter decreasing through GOAL_VALUE.

GOAL_TOLERANCE.description:
Convergence bar on the parameter value at the reported epoch, in the
parameter's own unit. A provider that cannot meet it returns
ROOT_REFINEMENT_FAILED rather than reporting an unconverged root.

OCCURRENCE.description:
Which attainment satisfies the condition, one-based. 0 and 1 both mean
the first.

PCEStopRequest.description:
Propagate until a condition is attained. The propagator itself is NOT named
here: it is a port the caller supplies, per the pluggable-propagation law.
This record carries only the condition, the interval and the tolerances.

CONDITIONS.description:
Conditions evaluated together; the run stops at whichever is attained
first in time.

MAXIMUM_ELAPSED_SECONDS.description:
Upper bound on the propagated interval. Reaching it without attaining a
condition is GOAL_NOT_ATTAINED, never a silent stop.

EPOCH_TOLERANCE_SECONDS.description:
Convergence bar on the stop epoch. The same scenario run at different
step sizes MUST land inside this bar.

SYNCHRONIZED_OBJECT_IDS.description:
Objects propagated in step with the owner and reported at the same stop
epoch.

REPORT_PARAMETERS.description: Parameters to evaluate at the stop epoch, beyond the condition itself.

PCEStopReport.description: Where a propagate-to-condition run actually landed.

UNKNOWN_PARAMETER.description: The name does not resolve in the publisher's catalog.

NOT_IMPLEMENTED.description: The name resolves and is DECLARED_UNAVAILABLE.

MISSING_DEPENDENCY.description: A coordinate system, central body, site or second object the parameter requires was not supplied.

OUT_OF_DOMAIN.description: The parameter is defined only on a regime this state is not in: a launch asymptote on a bound orbit.

BUDGET_EXCEEDED.description: The run hit its step or evaluation budget before answering.

ATTAINED_CONDITION_INDEX.description:
Index into PCEStopRequest.CONDITIONS of the condition that stopped the
run; negative when none did.

EPOCH.description: Epoch the run stopped at, ISO 8601.

EPOCH_TIME_SYSTEM.description: Time system of EPOCH, named by the $TIM timingStandard member name.

ELAPSED_SECONDS.description:
Seconds of propagated time from the initial state to EPOCH; negative for
a BACKWARD run.

ACHIEVED_VALUE.description: Value the condition parameter actually had at EPOCH.

GOAL_RESIDUAL.description:
ACHIEVED_VALUE minus GOAL_VALUE, in the parameter's own unit. This is
the residual a consumer gates on; it is NOT assumed to be zero.

SYNCHRONIZED_STATES.description: States of SYNCHRONIZED_OBJECT_IDS at the same epoch, in that order.

SAMPLE.description: Parameters evaluated at the stop epoch.

FUNCTION_EVALUATION_COUNT.description: Root-refinement work actually done, for the step-independence evidence.

PCE.description:
Parameter Catalog and Evaluation

The named calculation parameters an analysis resolves through: their owner
class, unit, data type, frame dependency and per-publisher availability
(CATALOG), a request and result for evaluating named parameters on states
at epochs in a stated coordinate system (EVALUATION_REQUEST /
EVALUATION_RESULT), and propagate-to-condition, which is a predicate on one
of those same names rather than a vocabulary of its own (STOP_REQUEST /
STOP_REPORT). Stopping conditions, targeting goals, report columns and plot
series all resolve names here, so a name means one thing everywhere.

Angles are radians, lengths metres, durations seconds, masses kilograms.
A buffer carries the members its exchange needs; a catalog publication and
an evaluation exchange are both complete $PCE records.

FrequencyRange.description: Frequency range with lower and upper limits

StokesParameters.description: Stokes parameters, representing different aspects of polarization

U.description: Another linear polarization, orthogonal to Q

Band.description: Table representing a frequency band with a name and frequency range

DATA_MODE.description: Mode of the data (real, simulated, synthetic)

EXERCISE.description: Data collected during an exercise scenario.

POWER_TYPE.description: Type of power (eg. AC or DC)

TRANSMIT.description: Indicates if the EMT can transmit

RECEIVE.description: Indicates if the EMT can receive

INFRARED_SENSOR.description: Electromagnetic Spectrum Sensors Detects infrared radiation

RADAR.description: Radar and Radio Telescopes Basic radar systems

PHASED_ARRAY_RADAR.description: Advanced radar with phased array technology

BISTATIC_RADIO_TELESCOPE.description: For astronomical observations using bistatic setup

ATMOSPHERIC_SENSOR.description: Environmental and Atmospheric Sensors For atmospheric studies

SEISMIC_SENSOR.description: Specialized Scientific Sensors For measuring seismic activities

LIDAR.description: Advanced Optical and Imaging Sensors Light Detection and Ranging

MULTISPECTRAL_SENSOR.description: Capturing image data at multiple wavelengths

HYPERSPECTRAL_SENSOR.description: Advanced imaging across many spectral bands

GPS_RECEIVER.description: Positioning and Tracking Sensors For Global Positioning System reception

RADIO_COMMUNICATIONS.description: Communication Devices Standard radio communication device

LASER_INSTRUMENT.description: Specialized Scientific Instruments Device for laser-based experiments and measurements

RF_ANALYZER.description: Radio frequency analysis and measurement device

LASER_IMAGING.description: Optical Devices Device for laser-based imaging

NAME.description: Display name of the owner or source the code stands for.

DESCRIPTION.description: Longer description of the owner or source.

ACTIVE.description: True while the code is in current use by the publishing catalogue.

SOURCE_URL.description: URL of the reference table the row was retrieved from.

RETRIEVED_AT.description: ISO 8601 UTC time the reference table was retrieved.

CATProduct.description: One product the catalog selected for the object, by content identifier.

RECORD_CID.description:
CIDv1 of the product record: a multihash (SHA-256) of its exact bytes as
published, a size-prefixed FlatBuffer.

SOURCE_ID.description: The product's source: its PROVENANCE SOURCE_ID.

EPOCH.description:
Epoch of the product, ISO 8601 UTC: an $OMM's EPOCH, an $OCM's first state
epoch.

SELECTION_REASON.description:
Why the catalog selected this product over the other candidates of its
KIND, as the selecting integrator states it (for example, the lowest
measured median error for the object's orbit regime and prediction
horizon).

STALE.description:
True when a maneuver after EPOCH retired the product and no product of its
KIND from after the maneuver has been selected yet.

OBJECT_TYPE.description: Object type (Payload, Rocket body, Debris, Unknown)

EUME.description: European Organization for the Exploitation of Meteorological Satellites (EUMETSAT)

LKA.description: Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka

MMR.description: Republic of the Union of Myanmar

PRES.description: People's Republic of China/European Space Agency

RCS.description: Radar Cross Section [meters2]; blank if no data available

ORBIT_TYPE.description: Orbit type (Orbit, Landing, Impact, Docked to RSO, roundtrip)

MANEUVERABLE.description: Indicates if the object is maneuverable

SIZE.description: Size [meters]; blank if no data available

MASS.description: Mass [kilograms]; blank if no data available

BUS_ID.description:
Join key to the BUS record describing this object's satellite bus; holds
that record's BUS.ID verbatim. MANUFACTURER, DIM_X/DIM_Y/DIM_Z, DRY_MASS
and WET_MASS are properties of the bus design and live on BUS — they are
NOT duplicated here. Empty when the bus is unknown.

CATALOG_URI.description:
Absolute URI identifying the original catalog's object-ID namespace.
This is an identifier, not an instruction to fetch a resource. Use with
CATALOG_OBJECT_ID only when both fields are present. Preserve the pair
through replicas and derived catalogs; it does not assert a NORAD or
COSPAR association. If the authority can reassign an object ID, this URI
must identify its immutable edition or assignment interval, rather than
the unversioned catalog. Stable IDs may use a persistent catalog URI.

CATALOG_OBJECT_ID.description:
Exact, opaque object identifier assigned by CATALOG_URI's authority.
Preserve case, Unicode and leading zeros. Numeric-looking native IDs
are not NORAD_CAT_ID values. Neither a matching name nor a native ID
in a different namespace establishes that two records describe the same
physical object. Publication provenance retains source and edition data.

PRODUCTS.description:
The products an integrating catalog selected for the object as of
PRODUCTS_AS_OF: one $OMM per mean-element theory, each with the $OCM of
the same source and epoch where there is one. The object's maneuvers are
its $MNV stream, not references here.

PRODUCTS_AS_OF.description: ISO 8601 UTC instant the selection in PRODUCTS holds at.

PPEPositionRecord.description:
A single time-segment record of polynomial coefficients for Cartesian position
(and optionally velocity). Coefficients are stored per axis.

To evaluate position at time t within this record's validity window:
1. Compute normalized time: tau = (t - EPOCH_MID) / EPOCH_HALF_SPAN
where tau is in [-1, +1].
2. Evaluate the polynomial basis of degree (NUM_COEFFICIENTS - 1) using
the coefficients for each axis.

Velocity coefficients, if present, follow the same evaluation procedure.
If HAS_VELOCITY_COEFFICIENTS is false, velocity can be obtained by
analytically differentiating the position polynomial.

EPOCH_MID.description:
Midpoint epoch of this record's validity window (ISO 8601 UTC or TDB).
Together with EPOCH_HALF_SPAN, defines the time interval:
[EPOCH_MID - EPOCH_HALF_SPAN, EPOCH_MID + EPOCH_HALF_SPAN]

EPOCH_HALF_SPAN.description:
Half-span of the validity window in seconds.
The full span is 2 * EPOCH_HALF_SPAN seconds centered on EPOCH_MID.

NUM_COEFFICIENTS.description:
Number of polynomial coefficients per axis.
The polynomial degree is (NUM_COEFFICIENTS - 1).
Typical values: 8-32 for high-fidelity ephemeris fits.

BASIS_TYPE.description: Polynomial basis type for interpreting the coefficient arrays.

CHEBYSHEV.description: Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind T_n(x). Most common for ephemeris fitting due to minimax approximation properties.

LEGENDRE.description: Legendre polynomials P_n(x). Orthogonal on [-1, 1] with unit weight function.

HERMITE.description: Hermite interpolating polynomials. Matches both function values and derivatives at nodes.

LAGRANGE.description: Lagrange interpolating polynomials. Exact interpolation through specified nodes.

POWER_SERIES.description: Standard power series (monomial basis): c0 + c1*x + c2*x^2 + ...

POS_COEFF_X.description:
Position coefficients for X-axis (km).
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS. Ordered c0, c1, ..., c_{N-1}.

POS_COEFF_Y.description:
Position coefficients for Y-axis (km).
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS.

POS_COEFF_Z.description:
Position coefficients for Z-axis (km).
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS.

HAS_VELOCITY_COEFFICIENTS.description:
Whether explicit velocity coefficients are provided.
If false, velocity should be derived by differentiating the position polynomial.

VEL_COEFF_X.description:
Velocity coefficients for X-axis (km/s). Optional.
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS if present.

MAX_POSITION_RESIDUAL.description: Maximum position fit residual over this segment (km). Optional quality metric.

RMS_POSITION_RESIDUAL.description: RMS position fit residual over this segment (km). Optional quality metric.

PPEOrbitalElementRecord.description:
A single time-segment record of polynomial coefficients for classical orbital elements.

The six classical elements are:
1. SMA or R_PERIAPSIS (size/shape) — see SIZE_SHAPE_TYPE
2. Eccentricity (dimensionless)
3. Inclination (degrees)
4. Right Ascension of Ascending Node / RAAN (degrees)
5. Argument of Periapsis (degrees)
6. Anomaly (degrees) — see ANOMALY_TYPE

Evaluation follows the same normalized-time procedure as PPEPositionRecord.

EPOCH_MID.description: Midpoint epoch of this record's validity window (ISO 8601 UTC or TDB).

EPOCH_HALF_SPAN.description: Half-span of the validity window in seconds.

NUM_COEFFICIENTS.description: Number of polynomial coefficients per element.

BASIS_TYPE.description: Polynomial basis type for interpreting the coefficient arrays.

CHEBYSHEV.description: Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind T_n(x). Most common for ephemeris fitting due to minimax approximation properties.

LEGENDRE.description: Legendre polynomials P_n(x). Orthogonal on [-1, 1] with unit weight function.

HERMITE.description: Hermite interpolating polynomials. Matches both function values and derivatives at nodes.

LAGRANGE.description: Lagrange interpolating polynomials. Exact interpolation through specified nodes.

POWER_SERIES.description: Standard power series (monomial basis): c0 + c1*x + c2*x^2 + ...

SIZE_SHAPE_TYPE.description: Parameterization of the first orbital element (SMA vs R_PERIAPSIS).

SMA.description: Semi-major axis (km). Standard for elliptical orbits.

R_PERIAPSIS.description: Radius of periapsis (km). Preferred for hyperbolic orbits.

ANOMALY_TYPE.description: Anomaly type for the sixth orbital element.

MEAN_ANOMALY.description: Mean anomaly (linear in time for Keplerian motion).

ECCENTRIC_ANOMALY.description: Eccentric anomaly (auxiliary angle in the Kepler equation).

COEFF_SIZE_SHAPE.description:
Coefficients for SMA or radius of periapsis (km).
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS.

COEFF_ECCENTRICITY.description:
Coefficients for eccentricity (dimensionless).
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS.

COEFF_INCLINATION.description:
Coefficients for inclination (degrees).
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS.

COEFF_RAAN.description:
Coefficients for RAAN (degrees).
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS.

COEFF_ARG_PERIAPSIS.description:
Coefficients for argument of periapsis (degrees).
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS.

COEFF_ANOMALY.description:
Coefficients for anomaly (degrees). See ANOMALY_TYPE for interpretation.
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS.

MAX_ELEMENT_RESIDUAL.description:
Maximum element fit residual over this segment. Optional quality metric.
Units depend on the element (km for SMA, degrees for angles, dimensionless for ecc).

RMS_ELEMENT_RESIDUAL.description: RMS element fit residual over this segment. Optional quality metric.

PPE.description:
Polynomial Ephemeris — top-level message containing metadata and
one or more polynomial coefficient records for a single space object.

A PPE message may contain position records, orbital element records, or both.
Records should be ordered chronologically by EPOCH_MID and should collectively
cover the time span [START_TIME, STOP_TIME] without gaps.

CENTER_NAME.description: Origin of the reference frame (e.g., EARTH, MOON, MARS).

TIME_SYSTEM.description: Time system used for all epochs in this message.

SCLK.description: Spacecraft Clock (receiver) (requires rules for interpretation in ICD)

A1.description: Atomic time scale of the reference atomic-time network, offset from International Atomic Time by the fixed constant A1 - TAI = 0.0343817 s exactly. Appended last; never reorder or reuse existing values.

START_TIME.description: Start of the total time span covered by this ephemeris (ISO 8601).

STOP_TIME.description: End of the total time span covered by this ephemeris (ISO 8601).

DEFAULT_BASIS_TYPE.description:
Default polynomial basis type for all records in this message.
Individual records may override this with their own BASIS_TYPE field.

CHEBYSHEV.description: Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind T_n(x). Most common for ephemeris fitting due to minimax approximation properties.

LEGENDRE.description: Legendre polynomials P_n(x). Orthogonal on [-1, 1] with unit weight function.

HERMITE.description: Hermite interpolating polynomials. Matches both function values and derivatives at nodes.

LAGRANGE.description: Lagrange interpolating polynomials. Exact interpolation through specified nodes.

POWER_SERIES.description: Standard power series (monomial basis): c0 + c1*x + c2*x^2 + ...

POSITION_RECORDS.description:
Array of position polynomial records.
Each record covers a time segment; together they span [START_TIME, STOP_TIME].

ORBITAL_ELEMENT_RECORDS.description:
Array of orbital element polynomial records.
Each record covers a time segment; together they span [START_TIME, STOP_TIME].

EPHEMERIS_SOURCE.description:
Generating ephemeris source, verbatim as the generator names itself
(e.g., a planetary ephemeris series designation, a numerical propagator
name and version, or an in-house tool identifier).

NOMINAL_SEGMENT_SPAN.description:
Fit span in seconds used to generate each polynomial segment.
Informational; actual spans are in individual records.

NOMINAL_NUM_COEFFICIENTS.description:
Nominal number of coefficients per segment.
Informational; actual counts are in individual records.

PROVENANCE.description: Where this polynomial ephemeris comes from and the terms it travels under.

NCDSegmentDescriptor.description:
One independently addressed segment inside a native container.

A segmented binary ephemeris is not a single span: each segment has its own
body pair, frame, numeric type and time bounds, and a reader must choose
among them. $OEM carries the STATES; this carries the segment DESCRIPTOR
that says which states came from where and what must be written back.

NAME.description: Segment name as recorded in the container.

TARGET_NAIF_ID.description: Integer body code of the segment target.

CENTER_NAIF_ID.description: Integer body code of the segment centre.

FRAME_NAIF_ID.description: Integer reference frame code of the segment.

FRAME_NAME.description: Reference frame name as recorded in the container.

SEGMENT_TYPE.description:
Numeric segment data type, verbatim. The evaluation rule is a property of
this number (for example, Chebyshev position with fixed interval, or
discrete states with Lagrange interpolation); it is carried as the
container's own integer so a rewrite is exact.

START_SECONDS_PAST_J2000_TDB.description:
Segment coverage start, seconds past J2000 in the barycentric dynamical
time scale, as stored in the container.

INITIAL_ADDRESS.description: First addressed element of the segment inside the file.

FINAL_ADDRESS.description: Last addressed element of the segment inside the file.

POLYNOMIAL_DEGREE.description:
Polynomial degree or record size the segment type parameterises, when the
type carries one.

NCDSP3Header.description: Header block of a fixed-column satellite position container (SP3).

FILE_TYPE.description:
Record content indicator, e.g. "P" for positions only, "V" with
velocities.

SATELLITE_SYSTEM.description: Satellite system indicator recorded in the header.

ORBIT_TYPE.description: Orbit type as recorded, e.g. fitted, extrapolated, broadcast, helmert.

DATA_USED.description: Data used to produce the file, as recorded.

COORDINATE_SYSTEM.description: Terrestrial reference frame name as recorded.

AGENCY.description:
Producing agency as recorded IN THE FILE. This is observed content, not a
classification.

TIME_SYSTEM.description: Time system as recorded in the header.

GPS_WEEK.description: Week number of the first epoch in the file's own week counter.

SECONDS_OF_WEEK.description: Seconds of week of the first epoch.

MODIFIED_JULIAN_DAY_START.description: Modified Julian Day of the first epoch.

FRACTIONAL_DAY.description: Fractional day of the first epoch.

NUMBER_OF_EPOCHS.description: Number of epochs declared in the header.

SATELLITE_ACCURACY_EXPONENTS.description:
Per-satellite accuracy exponents, parallel to SATELLITE_IDS. The accuracy
is POSITION_VELOCITY_BASE raised to this power.

POSITION_VELOCITY_BASE.description:
Base for the position and velocity standard-deviation exponents carried
per state in $OEM.

CLOCK_RATE_BASE.description: Base for the clock bias and clock rate standard-deviation exponents.

COMMENT.description: Header comment lines in file order.

NCDScenarioEpochContainer.description: Parameters of a scenario-epoch text container.

SCENARIO_EPOCH.description: Epoch that every record offset is measured from, ISO 8601.

TIME_SYSTEM.description: Time scale the scenario epoch is expressed in.

DISTANCE_UNIT.description: Distance unit of the records, e.g. "Meters", "Kilometers".

COORDINATE_SYSTEM.description: Named coordinate system of the records.

COORDINATE_AXES.description: Named coordinate axes, when stated separately from the system.

INTERPOLATION_SAMPLES_M1.description:
Interpolation order expressed as (samples - 1), which is how these
containers state it. Carried verbatim rather than converted, so a rewrite
reproduces the source exactly.

NUMBER_OF_EPHEMERIS_POINTS.description: Number of ephemeris points declared in the container.

SEGMENT_BOUNDARY_TIMES.description: Segment boundary offsets in seconds from SCENARIO_EPOCH, when present.

NCDCode500Header.description: Header words of a fixed-record binary ephemeris container.

SATELLITE_NAME.description: Object name as recorded in the header.

EPOCH_STEP_SECONDS.description: Uniform step between data records, seconds.

HEADER_WORDS.description:
The header record's packed words in file order, undecoded. A reader that
understands a word decodes it; a rewriter reproduces the record exactly
without having to.

NCD.description:
Native Container Descriptor.

The file-level facts of an ephemeris, attitude or tracking container that
are NOT properties of the messages inside it. $OEM, $AEM and $TDM carry the
states, attitudes and observations; none of them can carry the internal
file name, the comment area, the segment address ranges, the header accuracy
block or the interpolation order the source declared, because those describe
the CONTAINER. Without them a read-then-write cycle silently invents header
values, and a segmented binary file cannot be reproduced at all.

ONE record covers every container class rather than one record per format:
the file-level facts are the same kind of fact in each, and the
format-specific blocks are optional sub-tables selected by FORMAT. Only the
block matching FORMAT is populated.

SPK_DAF.description: Double-precision Array File container carrying Spacecraft and Planet Kernel segments: a binary file of typed, independently addressed ephemeris segments, each with an integer target and centre, an integer reference frame, a numeric segment type, and a contiguous address range inside the file.

SP3_C.description: SP3 version c: fixed-column text container of per-epoch satellite positions and optional velocities with a clock column, a header block of accuracy codes, and one uniform epoch interval.

SP3_D.description: SP3 version d: as SP3_C, with an unbounded satellite count and extended header lines.

CODE_500.description: Code-500 fixed-record binary ephemeris: a header record of packed words followed by fixed-length data records on a uniform step.

SCENARIO_EPOCH_EPHEMERIS_TEXT.description: Scenario-epoch ephemeris text container: time-ordered position and velocity records whose epochs are offsets in seconds from a declared scenario epoch, qualified by a named coordinate system, a distance unit, a named interpolation method and an interpolation order.

SCENARIO_EPOCH_ATTITUDE_TEXT.description: Scenario-epoch attitude text container: the attitude counterpart of SCENARIO_EPOCH_EPHEMERIS_TEXT, carrying quaternion, Euler or angular velocity records against the same scenario epoch.

CCSDS_OEM_KVN.description: CCSDS Orbit Ephemeris Message, keyword-value notation.

CCSDS_AEM_KVN.description: CCSDS Attitude Ephemeris Message, keyword-value notation.

CCSDS_TDM_KVN.description: CCSDS Tracking Data Message, keyword-value notation.

CCSDS_OMM_KVN.description: CCSDS Orbit Mean-Elements Message, keyword-value notation.

CCSDS_OPM_KVN.description: CCSDS Orbit Parameter Message, keyword-value notation.

CCSDS_OCM_KVN.description: CCSDS Orbit Comprehensive Message, keyword-value notation.

CCSDS_CDM_KVN.description: CCSDS Conjunction Data Message, keyword-value notation.

CCSDS_APM_KVN.description: CCSDS Attitude Parameter Message, keyword-value notation.

CCSDS_ACM_KVN.description: CCSDS Attitude Comprehensive Message, keyword-value notation.

CCSDS_RDM_KVN.description: CCSDS Reentry Data Message, keyword-value notation.

SENTINEL_EOF_XML.description: ESA Earth Explorer orbit file in XML (Sentinel-1, -2 and -3 AUX_POEORB, AUX_RESORB and AUX_PREORB).

NAIF_CK_DAF.description: NAIF C-kernel: a DAF holding pointing (attitude) segments.

PCK_DAF.description: NAIF binary Planetary Constants Kernel: a DAF holding body orientation as Chebyshev segments (data types 2, 3 and 20), with no size or shape data; e.g. the Moon's principal-axis frame in moon_pa_de440_*.bpc (NAIF, PCK Required Reading).

PROVIDER_DEFINED.description: A container outside this roster. PROVIDER_DEFINED_FORMAT_NAME states which; a producer never reuses a neighbouring member instead.

PROVIDER_DEFINED_FORMAT_NAME.description: Format name when FORMAT is PROVIDER_DEFINED. Empty otherwise.

FORMAT_VERSION.description: Version of the container format as declared by the file itself.

PRODUCER.description: Producing system or organization as recorded IN THE FILE.

CREATION_DATE.description: Creation date recorded in the file, ISO 8601.

INTERNAL_FILE_NAME.description:
Container-internal file name, which is stored inside the file and is
independent of the name on disk.

COMMENT_AREA.description:
Free-text comment area carried inside the container, one entry per line,
in file order.

NATIVE_FRAME_NAME.description:
Reference frame name as the container itself spells it, before any
mapping onto $RFM.

NATIVE_FRAME_ID.description: Integer reference frame code as the container stores it.

NATIVE_TIME_SYSTEM.description:
Time system as the container itself spells it, before any mapping onto
the ratified time-scale vocabulary.

SEGMENTS.description:
Descriptors of the container's segments, in file order. Empty for a
single-span container.

SP3_HEADER.description: Header block when FORMAT is SP3_C or SP3_D.

SCENARIO_CONTAINER.description:
Parameters when FORMAT is SCENARIO_EPOCH_EPHEMERIS_TEXT or
SCENARIO_EPOCH_ATTITUDE_TEXT.

CODE_500_HEADER.description: Header words when FORMAT is CODE_500.

START_TIME.description: Total coverage start across all segments, ISO 8601.

STOP_TIME.description: Total coverage stop across all segments, ISO 8601.

SOURCE_BYTE_LENGTH.description: Length of the described container in bytes.

SOURCE_SHA256.description:
SHA-256 of the described container's exact bytes, lowercase hex. This is
what makes the descriptor checkable: a consumer can prove the descriptor
belongs to the file it holds.

SOURCE_CID.description:
Content identifier of the described container when it is addressed by

Event Locator

One request and one report for every class of located event: shadow
passage, site visibility, sensor-field-of-view intrusion, apsis passage,
node crossing, and the generic condition on any $PCE catalog parameter.
Every class is the same pair of an event function and a refined root, so a
